title: BIND verification trusts replace refs, info/grafts and inherited GIT_* environment, so a forged merge reports VERIFIED_OFFLINE
evidence: On synthetic ledgers: (A1) version added by direct commit, then `git replace --graft <c2> <base> <c1>` -> apply_ledger(require_binding=True) returns effect APPLIED, bound_by 2. (A1b) same with .git/info/grafts. (A2) evil merge that alters decisions/R-v0001.md hidden behind `git replace <evil> <clean>` -> APPLIED. (A8) GIT_DIR pointing at another repository -> APPLIED although the real repository holds only a direct push. With GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 / GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null in the environment the same cases are rejected ('merge_commit has 1 parent(s)').
consequence: The controls the package claims for direct push, fast-forward and change-after-review are defeated by repository-local metadata that travels with a copied directory, a mirror clone or a bundle that includes refs/replace. A staged version becomes effective and the report says git: VERIFIED_OFFLINE.

title: Encoded non-ASCII look-alikes and controls are accepted; malformed UTF-8 is rejected only by accident in the path and accepted in the query
evidence: Accepted: /download/example/%EF%BC%8E%EF%BC%8E/other (fullwidth dots), %EF%BC%8Fother (fullwidth solidus), %E2%80%AE.pdf (bidi override), %C2%85 (C1 control), '..%20' and '.%20' segments, '...' segment, ?x=%C0%AE. Path %C0%AE%C0%AE is rejected only because urllib.parse.unquote raises UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError subclass); the reason shown is "'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xc0".
consequence: Handlers that apply compatibility or best-fit mapping, or strip trailing spaces and dots, can read these as dot segments or separators; the bidi and control escapes can mislead a human reviewer of a locator.
required_correction: Reject escapes >= 0x80 unless they decode as UTF-8 to an allowed category (no Cc, Cf, Zs; no NFKC change), in path and query alike, with an explicit reason; reject segments that are only dots and spaces.
